title: Control owner service is not stated in the controls catalog
source: Recovery Workbench Controls Catalog v3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Sheet Controls, columns Performed by, Evidence and How it is tested; version 4 columns O and P
description: The 44 control rows name a performer as a role or a monolith component, for example Rules component, Decision center, Decision log writer, Document hub and ACE access check, and name no service. Version 4 adds one primary owner service per control from the Ownership Map v1, chosen by the table, endpoint, event, workflow or job that the control reads or writes, with the basis in column P. No other cell of a control row changes.
evidence: Controls column Performed by: 44 rows, each a role, a system or a monolith component; no row names a service. Ownership Map v1 sheets Services, Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities, Jobs and Rulings give the owner per object; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the objects each of the 19 services owns.
proposed: Confirm the owner service of each of the 44 controls with the control owner and the service owner, and keep the owner basis column as the record of the ruling.

title: CTL-36 first runs in E5 while its owner service rwb-partner is wave 4
source: Recovery Workbench Controls Catalog v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Controls row CTL-36, column First in; Template and Rules R5.6 wave map; Ownership Map sheet Services
description: CTL-36, partner service levels and recoverable court fees, states First in E5. EP05 is wave 3 in the R5.6 wave map, while S9 rwb-partner, the service that owns panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees and scorecards, is created in wave 4. Version 4 keeps First in E5 word for word, records S9 rwb-partner as the owner service and raises this conflict. The other 43 controls map to a service whose wave is at or before the wave of their first release.
evidence: Controls CTL-36 column First in reads E5. Template and Rules R5.6: EP04 and EP05 are wave 3. Architecture v5 slide 41: S9 rwb-partner, wave 4. Ownership Map sheet Services: S9 rwb-partner, wave 4. Architecture v5 slide 17: InstructionWorkflow with SLA timers; S9 owns fees and scorecards; JOB-18 and JOB-19 are the only Temporal Schedules outside rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-comms, rwb-writeoff and rwb-payment.
proposed: Decide whether CTL-36 runs from wave 3 on partner instructions and fee data published by S9 through its contract and fake, or whether its first release moves to E6, where S9 rwb-partner exists; record the ruling in the Change Register.

title: Five controls check work that two services own
source: Recovery Workbench Controls Catalog v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Controls rows CTL-01, CTL-04, CTL-08, CTL-27 and CTL-31; version 4 columns O and P
description: Five controls check work held by more than one service: CTL-01 checks the case (P3 rwb-case) and the REC-01 to REC-05 reconciliation (P1 rwb-source-data); CTL-04 checks the approval (P7 rwb-decision) against the DoA limit (P4 rwb-access, delegation_limit); CTL-08 checks the rule package (P7) against reference loads and lists (P3 rwb-case) and DoA limits (P4); CTL-27 checks asset pricing and the re-appraisal schedule (S5 rwb-asset) against the valuation record (S1 rwb-valuation); CTL-31 checks the data tape (S6 rwb-debtsale) against the masking rule (P4). Version 4 records the service that holds the control record as primary owner and names the other owner in the basis column.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41: P3 owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation and timers; P1 owns the ACE view contract, freshness and reconciliation; P7 owns approvals and the central decision ledger; P4 owns roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table and access log; S5 owns assets taken on, holding, floor price and listings; S1 owns valuations; S6 owns lots and the data room. Ownership Map sheets Tables and Endpoints: reconciliation_result P1, approval P7, delegation_limit P4, rule_package P7, parameter_catalog and reference_row P3, listing S5, valuation records S1, masking_rule P4, debt_sale_lot S6.
proposed: Confirm for each of the five controls which service holds the control evidence and which service is tested, so that the control is written once in the test pack and appears against one story.

title: The conduct sample control has no owner in the Ownership Map
source: Recovery Workbench Controls Catalog v3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Controls row CTL-39; Ownership Map v1 sheets Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities and Jobs
description: CTL-39 checks a monthly sample of contacts, notices and decisions against the conduct rules and names the Conduct and QA officer as the performer. The Ownership Map has no conduct, QA sample or sample object, endpoint, event, workflow or job, so no service is fixed for it. Version 4 records P9 rwb-reporting, derived from the measures, snapshots and regulatory reports it owns and from the all-business-events projection, because the sample reads notices, interactions and decisions from events.
evidence: Controls CTL-39 columns Performed by and How it is tested: Conduct and QA officer; re-perform a sample; monthly. Ownership Map sheets Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities and Jobs contain no conduct or sample row. Architecture v5 slide 41: P9 owns measures, snapshots, steering dashboard and regulatory reports. Slide 15: rwb-reporting receives all business events as projections.
proposed: Confirm P9 rwb-reporting as owner of the conduct sample, or add the sample as a P9 measure and a P4 rwb-access review, and record the ruling in the Ownership Map before E8.

title: Control rows still name monolith components and monolith messages
section: Controls columns Performed by, Evidence and How it is tested
description: Rows name the monolith components Rules component, Decision center, Decision log writer, Document hub, ACE access check, Debt sale agent and Write-off agent, and the messages MSG-P7-002, MSG-P7-005, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P5-002, MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-S4-001, MSG-S2-001, MSG-S2-002 and MSG-S5-001 and MSG-S5-002. Version 4 keeps the wording word for word and records the service in column O, so a row states the realigned owner but still describes the check by its monolith name.
evidence: Controls column Performed by: Rules component (CTL-01, CTL-03, CTL-21, CTL-22, CTL-25, CTL-34, CTL-35, CTL-42), Decision center (CTL-04, CTL-05, CTL-07, CTL-23, CTL-24, CTL-26, CTL-28), Decision log writer (CTL-06), ACE access check (CTL-09), Document hub (CTL-12, CTL-13), Communications (CTL-14 to CTL-17), Debt sale agent (CTL-31), Write-off agent (CTL-33). Column How it is tested: MSG-P7-002, MSG-P7-005, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P5-002, MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-S4-001, MSG-S2-001, MSG-S2-002, MSG-S5-001 and MSG-S5-002.
proposed: In the next version, map each monolith component name and each MSG-Px-nnn code to the service and its API or event, keep the old wording in a preserved column, and confirm the mapping with the control owners.

title: No approval of version 4 is recorded
description: The source workbook has no approval row, no status cell and no signature block, and no approval of version 4 is recorded in any source of this run. Version 4 states Status: Draft and names this gap, and it keeps every control and count of version 3.
evidence: Controls Catalog v3: sheets Controls, By type, By release and Key, none with a status, approval or sign-off row. Template and Rules R8.1 requires the header lines and a change-log row; the run records no approval stop (R1 U8).
proposed: Record the approval of the Controls Catalog v4 by the control owner and the programme governance forum, and carry the approved status in the Read me sheet.

title: No calendar release date is stated for any control
source: Recovery Workbench Controls Catalog v3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
description: First in gives a business epic, E1 to E8, and no date. Version 4 keeps the epics and adds no date, so no release date of a control can be marked tentative. If a date is written into a later version it is tentative (R1 U7), and the programme date set is not stated in the catalog.
evidence: Controls column First in: E1 10, E2 12, E3 7, E4 2, E5 4, E6 4, E7 3, E8 2; no date cell in any sheet. Template and Rules R1 U7 and R5.6: release dates are tentative and unchanged, and a date is never raised as a gap.
proposed: When the programme date set is published, add the tentative release date beside each epic and mark it (tentative) without changing the epic.
